name: colRanges
title: Gets the range of values in each column of a matrix

origin.description: Gets the range of values in each column of a matrix.
origin.usage:
colRanges(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, dim. = dim(x),
  ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when not a matrix. The argument is named with a period so it does not clash with dim.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: The installed function returns a K by 2 matrix. Column 1 is the minimum and column 2 is the maximum, in the order of cols. Each column is scanned in the order of rows. When x is integer and every selected column has a non-missing value, the result stays integer. A column with no counted value makes the whole result double, with +Inf as the minimum and -Inf as the maximum. For doubles, R's NA stops that column. A plain NaN is stored and later finite values do not replace it.
origin.value: A K by 2 matrix. K is the number of columns for which the ranges are calculated. The mode is integer when x is integer and every column counted a value, and double otherwise.

translation.description: Gets the range of values in each column of a matrix.
translation.usage: colRanges(x, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False, dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A 1-d vector is accepted when dim is set; it is filled column-major, as R stores a matrix. Integer values stay on the integer path. Floating values are computed as float64. Logical input is rejected.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and logical values are recycled. The scan walks the selected rows in this order.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column. The result has one row per selected column, in this order.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are excluded. This is na.rm. False keeps R's NA and a plain NaN.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the number of rows and columns. This is dim. in R. None uses the shape of a 2-d x. A 1-d x is filled in column-major order.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. It must be TRUE or FALSE. The result is a plain array, with no names attached.

translation.details: The scan lives in the Rust crate colranges, ported from matrixStats src/colRanges.c with what 2 and hasNA TRUE. The result has two columns, the minimum and the maximum. R's NA is a NaN whose low 32 bits are 1954: that payload is copied and the rest of the column is skipped when na_rm is false. A plain NaN is stored, later finite values do not replace it, and a later NaN overwrites both columns with its own payload. A column with no counted value is +Inf and -Inf. Integer input returns int32 when every column counted a value. If any column counted nothing, the whole result is float64.
translation.value: An array of shape (K, 2). Floating input returns float64. Integer input returns int32 when every selected column has a non-missing value, and float64 otherwise.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.colranges import colRanges

x = np.arange(1, 13).reshape((4, 3), order="F")
colRanges(x)
